conventions.convention: Configurations are locally finite simple point sets with the bounded-Borel-count sigma-algebra. The reference Q is unit-intensity Poisson; its N-point sector is the pushforward of e^(−|D|)/N! times labelled product Lebesgue measure.

The pair potential is even, Borel, real or +∞, stable on every finite position list, and zero beyond Euclidean range R. Conditional energy includes interior pairs and interior-to-exterior pairs, but excludes exterior-only pairs. The vacuum energy is zero.
A continuum DLR law satisfies μγΛ=μ for every nonempty bounded Borel region; stationarity is not imposed by this definition. No infinite-volume existence or uniqueness is asserted.

Numerical parameters are β=E0βSI and z=ℓ0^d zc. The standard positional grand partition equals e^V times the normalized unit-Poisson partition, so their pressure rates differ by 1; in three dimensions physical pressure is E0p/(βℓ0³).

The eight limit clauses have separate hypotheses. Local equivalence concerns periodized spatial empirical fields, using outer probability for arbitrary open neighborhoods. The shrinking shell has a selected width. The β=0 clause retains hard exclusions and has no SI temperature or pressure interpretation.
The uniform one-body energy is varied while activity, temperature and reference scales remain fixed; pressure is defined by the thermodynamic logarithmic grand-partition rate.

load_bearing.statement: For every bounded Borel D, the unit-Poisson n-point sector is the pushforward of e^(−|D|)/n! times product Lebesgue measure. Under AC, stability, finite range and a locally finite exterior, e^(−|Λ|) ≤ ZΛη ≤ e^(−|Λ|) exp(z|Λ| exp(βB(1+2m))) < ∞. The resulting kernels are measurable, satisfy γΛγΔ=γΛ for Δ⊆Λ, and their fixed measures are exactly laws with the specified conditional interior distributions.
Defines stable finite-range continuum conditional energies, unit-Poisson-reference Gibbs kernels, their full-configuration extensions, and the DLR identity μγΛ=μ for every nonempty bounded Borel Λ.

Eight separate conditional conclusions cover stable power-tempered free-cube pressure; stable regular interior canonical rates and duality; superstable regular variational pressure; van Hove free-wall rates; free and periodic empirical-field concentration; one selected shrinking positional energy window; positive-core uniform tempered exterior pressure; and a separate retained-hard-exclusion β=0 continuation, each with its stated hypotheses.

concerns.concern: The Jansen source locator says 'Section 1.2, PDF pp.7–9: stability and superstable energy functions'. In the linked notes, Section 1.2 is instead 'Large deviations for Poisson and normal laws', beginning on printed p.8; the inspected passage concerns ideal-gas Poisson/Gaussian asymptotics. See [Jansen's notes](https://www.math.lmu.de/~jansen/gibbspp.pdf), contents and Section 1.2. The local zero-potential counterexample is sound, but this locator does not support its advertised subject.

Step 4.1 states 'for fixed ζ,η, the conditional density' is the Δ kernel. With +∞ interactions, the ζ-dependent remainder energy can be +∞, giving that ζ zero marginal weight under γΛ. The conditional-density assertion should be restricted to almost every ζ under the marginal, or derived directly by nonnegative factorization without dividing by a zero marginal density. The consistency conclusion survives this immediate qualification.

seams_checked.note: Checked the continuum-interaction definition, Gibbs physical parameters and adopted equilibrium/counting interfaces against their uses.
